dedupe_keys.name: dahiti hydrological time series of inland waters from satellite altimetry and imagery

description: DAHITI, the Database for Hydrological Time Series of Inland Waters, was started in 2013 by DGFI-TUM to publish water level time series for lakes, reservoirs, rivers and wetlands derived from multi-mission satellite altimetry, and it now also offers products from optical imagery. The home page lists the products: water levels from altimetry, surface areas from Landsat and Sentinel-2, volume variations for lakes and reservoirs, bathymetry above the minimum observed surface, water occurrence masks since 1984, land-water masks, hypsometric curves, water levels derived from hypsometry, river discharge and water surface slopes of rivers. The data holding table counts 29,359 targets in total, with the largest numbers in Europe and South America. All products are free after a short registration, and the page warns that the first API version was retired in mid-2024 in favour of version 2. Coverage: global inland waters that satellites can observe, at each satellite's revisit interval, not daily. Access: free with registration; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: small reservoirs and narrow rivers may not be observable, and target coverage differs by continent. It feeds reservoir storage, drought and flood-forecast simulations where gauge data are absent, and pairs with the GRanD dam records already in the catalogue.
